configs.description: The two-port unit with its external AC adapter. The brief lists "LM4-2S: LM4, 2 serial ports". The product page lists LM4-2S-NA, LM4-2S-UK and LM4-2S-EU, which differ by the power cord and adapter plug. It is drawn with four jacks like the four-port unit, so its export lists four ports. That is a drawing choice and not the maker's count of two. The brief lists a serial port activation licence.
configs.name: ac-2s

configs.description: The four-port unit with its external AC adapter. The brief lists LM4-4S and says AC plug options are available. The product page lists LM4-4S-NA, LM4-4S-UK and LM4-4S-EU, which differ by the power cord and adapter plug. They are not drawn as separate builds.
configs.name: ac-4s

gaps.note: The photograph shows a black four-position housing at the lower left of the front. A latch tab is above it and a direct-current mark under it. The brief gives the input range and the adapter's output, and names no connector. No interface is known, so no part is placed and the position is left bare. A connector is a part, so it is not drawn as decor.
gaps.wanted: the maker's name for the DC input connector, its pitch and the plug that mates it, from a hardware guide.

gaps.note: No held document shows the rear.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or a drawing of the rear of the LM4.

gaps.note: The positions are read from an angled photograph. Those read from threshold masks hold to about 1 mm, the error of the four estimated control points. In the same image the plate's lower edge reads 1.8 to 2.4 mm below the face's lower edge. Its top edge reads about 2 mm above the face's top edge. Together the plate reads up to about 4.4 mm taller than the face's 44.45 mm. The front's y figures may be stretched by up to about 10 percent. After the parts were moved to their measured places these differences remain. The button's centre is 0.4 mm left and 0.2 mm low. The serial jacks read about 16.5 mm wide against the part's 12.7, and a placement cannot change a part's width. Their lamps read about 3 mm wide against the part's 2.0. Each jack stands on the centre of its opening. The USB openings read about 6.2 mm tall against the part's 4.5. Every other position is read by eye and its error was not measured.
gaps.wanted: a straight front elevation or a hardware guide figure with dimensions.

gaps.note: No held LM4 document describes a lamp or a button. The photograph shows a lit green lamp on the left and a lit yellow lamp on the right of the console and serial jacks. The lamps are drawn in their off state by default. Their on states carry the colours the photograph shows, which a viewer sets. With a strict mask, serial green is 5464 px, mean (77,132,76), and serial yellow 4098 px, mean (189,172,16). Console green is 1159 px, mean (106,134,90), and console yellow 793 px, mean (148,138,51); a looser mask read them, so they are less certain. A second sample of the serial yellow with a looser mask came out darker, so that figure depends on the mask. The three small status lamps are dark in the photograph and are drawn off.
gaps.wanted: a table of what the three lamps and the round button show and do, and the marks beside them.

gaps.note: The registered mark sits at the upper right of the wordmark and reads about 2.1 mm across. Its ring is about 9 px across in the photograph and its letter about 4 px. That is too small to place honestly. The logo zone covers its place.
gaps.wanted: a larger photograph of the wordmark, to place the registered mark beside it.

gaps.note: The product page lists "Rack Mount Ear" in the box. No held document shows it or says where it fits.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the rack mount ear and the screw positions.

gaps.note: The lid draws six ridges in seven slots and the left flank three screws, from views at a grazing angle. They are estimated, to about 2 mm across and about 5 mm in depth. The photograph shows nothing of the right flank or the underside, so those two draw the envelope only. A straight picture of the lid and the flanks would place every feature on them.
gaps.wanted: photographs of the lid, the underside and both flanks.

body.note: The photograph shows a black front plate and lid and a silver left flank with three screws. At the top left of the front it shows a heatsink block of six fins and seven slots. The fins read 1.3 mm wide at a pitch of 4.6 mm. They come from the dark and grey runs of one row of the resampled photograph. The row at y 6.0 gives six runs of 1.25 to 1.3 mm. The colours are read from the photograph. The plate reads (67,65,70) over 92800 px, but unevenly: about (71,69,74) at the left and (31,29,28) at the right, in shadow. The drawn plate is #2b2e33 and stays, between the two. In the photograph the console jack and the two USB-A ports sit in one pale housing block. The four serial jacks sit in another, with a band between the two rows. They are drawn as two rectangles in the housing colour behind the parts. The housing colour reads (229,217,207), #e5d9cf, over 270177 pale pixels counted inside the two blocks themselves. The console block gives 122619 px at (226,216,209). The serial block gives 147558 px at (231,217,205). The six RJ45 jacks (E1, the console and the four serial jacks) are drawn in that colour through their finish field. E1's shell was not counted. The two USB-A ports show a dark grey tongue with a small pale slider at the lip, (33,32,32) over 12320 px. The drawn tongue is pale where the photograph's is dark. For a device that does not claim 3.0 the library's skin for this port is the white one, usb2. Its other skin is blue. Neither is dark. The skin matches in colour at the opening and not at the tongue. It is not a statement of the USB version, which the brief does not give. The right flank, the underside and the rear are not shown. The LANTRONIX wordmark is a logo and is not drawn: its place is the region logo-zone, read from the photograph. The plain text LM4 stays. The button and the four corner screws are round in the photograph and are drawn round, by a corner radius of half their side. The screws read about 5.6 mm across and the button 7 mm. The lid carries six ridges in seven slots at the left, read as 1.3 mm wide at a pitch of 4.6 mm like the front's. The left flank carries three round screws about 5.8 mm across, level at about 22.5 mm from the lid.

console.note: LM4 product brief: "one RS-232 console port", "Two USB-A ports". The jack at the top of the column of three carries a prompt mark and is the console jack. The two USB-A ports are under it. The brief does not say what either USB port is for beyond "an external cellular modem connected over USB" on page 2.

layout-source.note: The only picture of the front is the angled photograph on page 1 of the brief. It is 1550 x 1358 px and was taken from the left and above. The four corner screws are the control points of a projective map to the 158.75 by 44.45 mm face. Their place on the face is itself read from the plate edges in the same photograph. It is 4.5 mm in from each side and 3.6 mm from top and bottom. The screw centres, re-read in the native photograph, are top-left 383,725, top-right 1029,619, bottom-left 383,897 and bottom-right 1029,777 (x,y in px). The left screws are 172 px apart and the right screws 158 px apart. The photograph was resampled to the face at 20 px per mm. The heatsink opening, its fins, the legend bars and the logo zone were then read from threshold masks on that image. So were the two pale housing blocks, the screws, the lamps, the marks, the jacks, E1, the SFP cage and the colours. The edge blur is about 0.2 mm. The control points are themselves estimated, so every figure keeps about 1 mm of the method's own error. In the same image the plate's lower edge reads 1.8 to 2.4 mm below the face's lower edge. The front's y figures may be stretched by up to about 10 percent; the front-positions gap gives the two edges. Every other position is read by eye from the photograph. The placements were made from an earlier reading of the same four screws, within 7 px of these. The rows of each column are drawn level where the photograph reads them 1.5 mm apart. The photograph's serial jacks read about 16.5 mm wide, shell included, and the ganged jack part is 12.7 mm wide. A placement cannot change a part's width. Each part is placed on the centre of its photographed opening. The lid and the left flank were resampled the same way, with corners read from the photograph's own edges. The lid is seen at a grazing angle. Its figures hold to about 2 mm across and about 5 mm in depth, and are estimated.

leds.note: The photograph shows three small lamps in a level row and a round button. Under each lamp is a mark: a power mark, a pulse mark and a warning triangle. The lamp centres and the button colour are read from the photograph. No document says what a lamp shows or what the button does. The photograph shows more marks. Above E1 is a network icon and above E2 an antenna icon. Beside E1 and E2 are a link icon and an arrows icon. The console jack has a prompt icon in a boxed outline. To the right of the serial jacks is a "10101" mark. Under the four-position housing is a DC mark. Each is drawn as a silkscreen path, simplified, in the mean colour of its pixels. Its place and size are read from the resampled photograph. The link icon and the lower arrow run past the face's lower edge under that map. They are moved up by 1.6 and 1.0 mm to stay on the face. The photograph also shows a larger dark hole between the lamps and a small dark dot on each side of the SFP. They are drawn as round dark decor. The small dark dot inside each box of the network icon is not drawn. The registered mark beside the wordmark is not drawn. Its ring reads about 9 px across and its letter about 4 px in the photograph.

mount.note: The maker's product page lists "Rack Mount Ear" and "2 Mounting Screws" in the box. The brief calls the unit small and for IDFs and kiosks. No document shows an ear, a bracket or a position, so the unit is stated as a desktop device.

network.note: LM4 product brief: "One 10/100/1000 BaseT Ethernet interface" and "One 1-Gbps SFP port". The photograph prints E1 under the RJ45 jack and E2 under the SFP cage. The maker's product page says "2 Ethernet Ports" for each model, which counts the two.

power.note: LM4 product brief: "DC input: 9 to 60 VDC" and "Power consumption: Less than 24W". The external AC to DC supply reads "AC Input: 100-240VAC, 50-60HZ, 1.4A" and "DC Output: 12VDC, 3A". The photograph shows a four-position connector at the lower left of the front, over a direct-current mark. No document names its type, pitch or the plug that mates it, so it is not drawn as a part.

serial.note: LM4 product brief: "Supports up to 4 devices via serial (RS-232)". The photograph shows four RJ45 jacks in two rows of two numbered 1 and 2 over 3 and 4 under blue bars. The LM-Series fact sheet says the ports are "RJ-45 wired as DCE". It does not name the LM4. The brief lists "LM4-2S: LM4, 2 serial ports" and a "1 serial port activation" licence. Every build is drawn with four jacks, so the LM4-2S export lists four ports. That is a drawing choice and not the maker's count of two.

size.note: Lantronix LM4 product brief (MPB-00246 Rev A), page 2, System Specifications, Dimensions and Weight. It prints "44.45 mm (1.75 in.) x 158.75 mm (6.25 in.) x 158.75 mm (6.25 in.)" as height, width and depth.

storage.note: The maker's product page for the LM4 prints "16GB eMMC flash memory supporting TCG Opal 2.0, 256-bit AES encryption" as the on-board storage. The brief and the fact sheet do not print this line.
